shouldFix.why: This corpus treats advisory disposition as part of the decision's form, and the draft's own header claims 'Same form as the adopted set D-013 / D-015 / D-035 / D-042 / D-103 / D-104 / D-105 / D-106 / D-107 / D-108 / D-109.' I checked that claim against the adopted set: D-105 records 'Advisories CLAUDE-V8-A1 (ADV-V8-01: memberApplicability...)'; D-108, the immediately preceding decision, records 'Advisories CLAUDE-V14-A1, CODEX-V14-A1, and ...' and additionally carries its own turn-1 advisories; D-104 records three by id as travelling honesty work. Every adopted decision in this run that cited a verdict bearing advisories both named the count in the measured-inputs row and dispositioned them in the Decision block, in the settled form 'travel as honesty work'. D-110 does neither, so three items the reviewer explicitly rated advisory become unowned: no successor is told they are outstanding, and O-1 in particular is owed at DR-G20 authoring, which is exactly where it will be needed.
shouldFix.whyNotAMustFix: Nothing in the draft is false. The table says 'ACCEPT, 0/0', which is true on its own terms - both verdicts do carry 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX - and the draft never asserts that zero advisories exist. The ACCEPT gate is met, advisories do not block a recording, and the operative decision is correct and complete on every other check I ran. This is an omission from the record, not a misstatement of it.
shouldFix.likelyCause: Not carelessness so far as I can tell, but a field-name artifact worth naming because it will recur: Codex's verdict exposes an explicit 'advisories' array and Claude's does not, filing the same content under 'observations'. A coordinator scanning cited verdicts for an 'advisories' key would correctly find none on the Claude side and conclude there was nothing to disposition.
shouldFix.remedy: Annotate the Claude 2 row as 'ACCEPT, 0/0, 3 advisory observations O-1/O-2/O-3' and add the settled clause to the Decision block - that the three travel as honesty work on a successor and do not prevent this recording - in the same form D-104, D-105, D-108 and D-109 use. No other change is needed; the recording itself stands. If the coordinator prefers a general fix, reading advisory residue by severity rather than by field name would close the class for future cycles where a reviewer files under 'observations'.

summary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. All five measured rows reproduce byte-exactly, including a COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md pin that is current at HEAD 2d5f15b rather than inherited stale, and every dispatch attack fails: no positive SATISFIED or QUALIFIED, no implementation authorization, no SDK API chosen, G20 correctly NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED, DR-110 correctly distinguished from D-110, and all eleven cited precedents adopted. The single finding is an omission: the Claude 2 verdict carries three advisory observations, O-1 through O-3, which its own verdictBasis counts as 'Three advisory observations, none blocking', and the draft neither records nor dispositions them - breaking the practice every adopted decision in this run follows. Annotating the verdict row and adding the settled travel-as-honesty-work clause discharges it.
